items.title: 10.27 Winkler method, BOD and DO (numbered 10.27 as printed)

source_refs.note: Topic printed as 10.27 (10.23 to 10.26 are absent) with Figure 10.12, printed pages 239-240; the exercise is not reproduced.

blocks.text: Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) is the capacity of organic matter in natural water to consume oxygen within a period of five days. The value of BOD is the amount of oxygen consumed as a result of biological oxidation of dissolved organic matter in the sample. The oxidation reaction is catalyzed by microorganisms which are already present in the natural water. It is measured experimentally through Winkler method by calculating the concentration of oxygen at the beginning and at the end of five days period, in which a sealed water sample is maintained in the dark at constant temperature at 25°C.

blocks.alt: Graph of concentration against direction of flow of river. Dissolved Oxygen (solid line) is high, falls suddenly to a minimum and then rises slowly back to a high level. BOD (dotted line) is low, rises steeply at the same point to a peak and then falls gradually, crossing the dissolved oxygen curve.
blocks.caption: Figure 10.12: Inverse relationship between BOD and DO (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 10.12).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 10.12 spells ‘Disolved Oxygen’; the correct spelling is Dissolved Oxygen.

Dissolved oxygen (DO) is defined as the amount of oxygen dissolved in water. It is dissolved either from the atmosphere or released by plants during photosynthesis in water. Its concentration is between 5 to 8 mg/dm³. The minimum level of DO should be 5 mg/dm³. Below 5 mg/dm³, the water supposed to be polluted.

Dissolved Oxygen (DO) and Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) have an inverse relationship as shown in Figure 10.12. As bacteria consume oxygen in the water while decomposing organic matter, BOD increases, leading to lower dissolved oxygen (DO) level.

Winkler method is a technique used to measure the amount of dissolved oxygen (DO) in water samples. It is based on the idea that dissolved oxygen (DO) in the sample solution, has oxidizing properties and reacts with KI. The amount of iodine formed is measured by titrating with sodium thiosulfate using starch as an indicator which turns the solution dark blue, indicating the endpoint. The amount of iodine formed is proportional to the amount of dissolved oxygen in the solution.
